full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, that the present opposite party No. 1 as pre-emptor instituted the original Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case being No. 60 of 2003 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Dakop, Khulna under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 contending inter alia that the case joie appertaining to Mouza Dhopadihi under S.A. khatian No. 63 ad 68 comprising an area of .99 acres of land originally belonged to one Kali Charan Sarder in 08 annas share who died leaving behind his two sons Ajit Sarder and Jagadish Sarder. Ajit Sarder subsequently purchased 61/2 decimals of land on 24.05.1983 from the case holding. The pre-emptor by a sub-kabala deed dated 12.07.1977 purchased 50 decimals of land from Jagadish in the case holding and by virtue of this purchase he became a co-sharer by purchase in the case holding. At the demise of Ajit Sarder, his two sons the opposite party No. 3 and 4 became the heirs and the opposite party No. 2 behind the back of the pre-emptor transferred 99 decimals of land in favour of the purchaser-opposite party No. 1 who is a stranger purchaser to the case jote. The pre-emptor initially by a bainapatra acquired 49 decimals of land from the opposite party No. 3 and finally through a decree of a specific performance of contract in Suit No. 103 of 2000 he got the transfer deed registered. The further case of the pre-emptor is such that the pre-emptor for the time came to learn about the case kabala through her husband on 04.08.2003 and after getting the certified copy of the kabala on 07.08.2003 filed the original pre-emption miscellaneous case for getting the case land pre-empted. 

 3. The contrary case of the purchaser-opposite party No.1 in short is thus that Kalicharan Sarder being the owner of 08 annas share in S.A. Khatian No. 63, 65 & 68 died leaving the property in favour of his two sons and the two sons Ajit Sarder and Jagadish Sarder after the death of their father inherited that portion of land. Subsequently, Ajit Sarder died leaving behind two sons the opposite party No. 3 and 4 along with 04 daughters the opposite party No. 1 and others. The opposite party No. 1 and opposite party No. 4 purchased 501/4 decimals of land from their brother, the opposite party No. 3 on 29.08.1995. The opposite party No. 2 initially proposed to sale the case land in favour of the pre-emptor, but the pre-emptor wanted to give less price of the actual and thereafter the opposite party No. 2 sold the case land in favour of the opposite party No. 1 at proper consideration money and handed over possession therein, but the pre-emptor on false allegation filed the case.
